title: Hold an oxford shoe steady on an entry mat while inserting and seating a spring-loaded cedar shoe tree
instruction: Seat the twin-tube cedar shoe tree inside the oxford shoe on the entry mat, keeping the shoe upright on the mat and leaving both grippers clear.
context: Putting cedar shoe trees into leather dress shoes at the entryway after daily wear flattens vamp creases and absorbs moisture overnight. Because a twin-tube shoe tree is 14 mm longer than the shoe cavity and requires 5.5 N of spring compression to tuck its heel block beneath the curved heel collar while an unheld 380 g leather outsole slides at under 0.5 N on the smooth mat, one arm must brace the shoe while the other threads the forepart, compresses the tubes, and seats the heel.
setup: A fixed dark entryway shoe mat (360 x 560 x 5 mm, 2.5 mm perimeter curb, friction 0.12) rests centred at (0.310, 0.000) m on the station tabletop. On its inner half sits an unbolted size-10 right cap-toe oxford dress shoe (305 x 108 mm footprint, 84 mm heel width, 70 mm rear heel counter, 90 mm laced saddle, 380 g, friction 0.12) pointing along +y at (0.250, 0.042) m: a 16 mm outsole, welt, and calfskin insole deck bounds a 278 mm internal cavity from the front toe stop (+139 mm) to the rear heel-counter wall (-139 mm), with an 84 mm clear forepart chamber under a 62 mm cap-toe ceiling (rising to 72 mm below the 28 mm wide closed-lacing saddle), a 50 mm tapered cap-toe nose ahead of 68 mm outer brogue shoulders, ankle quarters dipping to 45.5 mm, and a 70 mm rear heel counter (66 mm clear pocket width) whose top collar (52 to 70 mm high) curves 8 mm forward to -131 mm (270 mm clear throat opening). Beside it at (0.370, 0.005) m rests a twin-tube spring-loaded red cedar shoe tree (292 mm uncompressed length, 320 g total: 145 g contoured cedar forepart 68 mm wide with twin 12 mm brass-toned guide tubes, and 175 g rounded cedar heel slide 54 x 44 x 32 mm with a 28 x 36 mm upright grip crest rising to 72 mm and a 44 mm front bolster) coupled by a 42 mm telescoping tube spring of stiffness 250.0 N/m (5.5 N at 22 mm compression, friction 0.58). One fixed starting layout; arms start at ready pose.
scoring: Judged statelessly at the end of the trial from observable end-state geometry; the run succeeds once 1.0 holds for 3 s. Measured in real trials with a caliper/ruler and digital protractor. 1.0: both the shoe and the shoe tree remain on the entry mat inside a 20 mm edge margin, the shoe rests upright within 10 deg on the mat (within 8 mm vertically of the mat surface and 65 mm horizontally of its starting mark), the cedar forepart tip sits at least 122 mm forward in the shoe cavity (within 18 mm laterally, 10 to 30 mm above the outsole bottom, aligned within 12 deg and rolled at most 15 deg), the heel block rear base sits 125 to 144 mm aft in the heel counter pocket (within 18 mm laterally and 10 to 30 mm above the outsole bottom, beneath the 52 mm collar lip) with 8 to 24 mm of active spring compression locking it in place, and both grippers' tool points and pad tips are at least 80 mm clear of both the shoe and the shoe tree. 0.70: fully seated and preloaded on the mat, but a gripper is still within 80 mm. 0.35: shoe upright on the mat with the forepart seated in the vamp, but the heel is unseated or resting on the collar rim or spring preload is outside 8 to 24 mm. 0 otherwise (doing nothing, hovering, pushing one-handed so the unbraced shoe slides without compressing past the collar, sweeping, or dropping off the mat). Possible scores: 0.0, 0.35, 0.70, 1.0.
reset_notes: Compress the cedar shoe tree forward by its upright heel crest, lift the heel block clear of the 52 mm heel collar lip, withdraw the forepart from the vamp, and place the oxford shoe at (0.250, 0.042) m and the uncompressed shoe tree at (0.370, 0.005) m on their reference marks on the entry mat.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (PhysX, 20 Hz control, SelfCollisions=False within articulations). The entry mat, oxford shoe, cedar forepart, and cedar heel slide are compound rigid bodies with measured masses, tuned PBR surface roughness/metallic, and dry friction; the twin telescoping spring tubes use one 42 mm prismatic slide joint (250.0 N/m, 5.5 N at 22 mm) with zero scripted welds or latches. Leather upper flex and moisture absorption are not modelled.
